description: The organisation's contract with the platform; examples/cluster.yaml is the whole file an organisation keeps. Anything not listed here is refused, so a typo is a refused HelmRelease with a message rather than a misspelt variable serving nobody.

domain.description: Public DNS suffix. Every application is a subdomain of it: docs.<domain>, id.<domain>.

storageClass.description: StorageClass for every persistent volume the platform creates.

ip.description: The shared Gateway's address: a MetalLB pool address, or what the cluster's load balancer allocates.

tlsIssuer.description: ClusterIssuer for the one SAN certificate.

acmeEmail.description: Let's Encrypt's contact for the certificate.

extraCertificates.description: TLS Secrets in office-system for hosts routed outside the platform; the Gateway picks one by SNI.

size.description: small (5-50 people, one node), medium (50-500, the measured one), large (500-5,000, HA; a shape, not a measurement). apps/README.md (Sizing) is what each means; every app carries its three sizes in apps/<app>/sizes/.

apps.description: Which apps run: `<app>: true|false`. An app not named takes its `default` from charts/control-plane/apps.yaml, the list of what exists; a name the table lacks is refused. Disabling an app removes it and keeps its data: database, role, passwords and bucket live in the platform layer, which provisions every app whether enabled or not, so re-enabling reconnects to them. Dependencies are enforced (drive needs collabora, docs needs find, meet needs docs; livekit follows meet). Messages is off by default: it needs port 25 open in both directions and a PTR record for its egress address (apps/messages/README.md, Mail DNS).

mode.description: garage: the platform runs its own S3 and publishes s3.<domain> for Drive's browser uploads. external: the organisation's S3 provider; endpoint, region and credentials come from a Secret `object-store` in office-data, applied by hand once like the SMTP relay (docs/install.md). Buckets are named after the apps and must exist before the first release, and Drive's needs CORS for https://drive.<domain>, which the platform cannot set on a store it does not run.

cluster.description: What the platform installs because the cluster lacks it (adr/0112). Off means the cluster brings its own, and preflight.py checks that it does.

install.description: Envoy Gateway, with the Gateway API CRDs.

className.description: The GatewayClass the Gateway attaches to.

kind.description: metallb: the Gateway pinned to gateway.ip. none: the cluster allocates.

configured.description: false ships a placeholder relay so every app starts; sends fail until the real Secret exists and this is true (docs/install.md, Mail).

monitoring.description: Alerts on what users notice (adr/0119). platform: the platform runs Prometheus and Alertmanager in office-monitoring and mails alerts to `email`. external: the cluster's own Prometheus operator picks up the platform's rules and probes, and routes them itself. none: nothing; preflight.py says so.

email.description: Where alerts go, through the platform's SMTP relay. Only under platform: under external the cluster's Alertmanager routes them.

source.description: Where the platform's source is fetched from, at the tag of this chart's version: this repository, or a fork of it.

secretRef.description: A Flux git Secret in flux-system for a private repository (`flux create secret git`); empty for a public one.

reconcile.description: Interval, retry interval and timeout of every Kustomization the control plane renders.
